title: Banking, Loans and Financial Safety
summary: UPI and OTP fraud, loans and interest, CIBIL, recovery agents, credit cards and income tax basics.
sectionRefs: Reserve Bank of India - Fair Practices Code and recovery agent rules

body.text: Most banking fraud does not need hacking. It only needs you to trust a caller, click a link, or share an OTP. Knowing a few rules keeps your money safe.
Protect your money: UPI and OTP

items: Never share your OTP, PIN, CVV or password with anyone. No bank or official will ever ask for them.
A request to 'receive money' never needs your PIN. Entering a PIN sends money out.
Do not scan a QR code to receive money.
Do not install screen-sharing or remote-access apps for a 'bank officer'.
Check your statement regularly.

body.text: If money leaves your account without consent

items: Inform your bank immediately and ask them to freeze the account and dispute the transaction.
Call the cyber helpline 1930 and report on cybercrime.gov.in.
Give the bank a written complaint and get an acknowledgement.
If it is unresolved, complain to the RBI Ombudsman.
Read the loan agreement: interest rate, EMI, processing fee, prepayment penalty and foreclosure terms.
Interest can be fixed or floating; a floating rate changes with the market.
A guarantor is legally liable to pay if the borrower defaults. Never sign as a guarantor casually.
Your CIBIL score reflects your repayment history and affects whether you get a loan, and at what rate.
Check your credit report regularly for errors and for loans opened in your name fraudulently.

body.text: What recovery agents can and cannot do

items: Recovery agents may contact you to recover a loan, but they cannot threaten, abuse or harass you or your family.
They must not use force, and must not contact you at unreasonable hours.
If you are harassed, complain to your bank and to the RBI Ombudsman.
Check your statement for hidden charges, annual fees and interest on unpaid balances.
Use only RBI-regulated digital lending apps. Unregulated apps can be predatory and misuse your data.
Form 16 (from your employer), AIS and Form 26AS show your income and the TDS already deducted.
If your income is above the basic exemption limit, you generally must file an income tax return.
File on the official portal incometax.gov.in. Never pay a 'tax agent' to a personal account.

body.text: Missed calls and messages that create urgency ('your account will be blocked') are a common trick. Slow down and verify through the official app or branch.
RBI rules limit your liability for unauthorised electronic transactions, but only if you report quickly. Delay can increase your own loss.
Keep the SMS, email and complaint reference numbers. They are proof of when you reported.

practicalSteps: Never share OTP, PIN, CVV or passwords.
Report a fraudulent transaction to your bank within the shortest possible time.
Read the loan agreement before signing, and never become a guarantor without understanding the risk.
Escalate to the RBI Ombudsman if the bank does not resolve your complaint within 30 days.
exceptions: If the fraud happened because you shared your credentials or were grossly negligent, your liability may be higher.
Some delays in reporting can shift more liability to you under RBI rules.

faqs.q: Will the bank refund my money?
faqs.a: If you report quickly and were not negligent, RBI rules support limited or zero liability. The bank must resolve your complaint within a set time.

faqs.q: Can a recovery agent call me at any time?
faqs.a: No. Agents must follow RBI rules on conduct and timing. Threats or harassment can be reported to your bank and the RBI Ombudsman.

misconceptions.myth: If the bank's app shows the transaction, I cannot dispute it.
misconceptions.fact: You can and should dispute any transaction you did not authorise, in writing, to the bank.
